questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I study law, so going to an EU country was important to me. That English is a first language was a plus, as I have found it very easy to engage with local culture. Gaining knowledge of a common law system was very appealing.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty ease. The process up to arriving I found that the coordinators in Cork were not always very helpful and would sometimes wave off your questions but once I got here the introduction and the help were all very accessible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a whole introduction week for visiting students with an introduction to how the system worked, how to finalize classes, and everything Erasmus related which was really nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was referred through my university as finding housing on my own was almost impossible. When I looked 4 months in advance almost all 1-semester options were fully booked.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Both on and off campus housing is very expensive. And it is expected that you further buy everything from duvets, towels, toilet bins to all things you need for cooking and cleaning.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a registration online before arrival and a confirmation at the physical office once you arrived and then you registered for classes. Registering for classes was a long process the classes started before you were approved for them and many courses weren't available even though they were when you originally chose.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: For registering general you could email the coordinator. For help with registering for classes it was a bit harder as the coordinators did not have all the information and you mostly just had to wait until classes had been going for a few weeks before getting approved.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There were two out of five classes that I didn't get and had to find new ones and one was solely online.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try and be okay with not getting all the classes you hoped for. It will be fine and they are very helpful even though the system is slow.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Mixed courses, some graduate courses as there where limited options available for law, some post graduate and some offered as legal LLM's and some non-legal LLM courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. Very lecture based. It was not expected that you had read for class and the text where not discussed but mainly seemed to be for the essays. Almost no discussion or questions but only passive listening. Many lecturers didn't engage but simply did a talk with a break some not even really using the slides they made available.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to International Law of the Sea, Public Law, Economic Law of the European Union, Sources and Foundations of Environmental Law, International Environmental Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Economic Law of the European Union was very interesting for me and the lecturer was passionate about it and kept a decent structure of the class. Public Law was a great way to get a basic introduction to the Irish system, legal and political, and common law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy all kitchen appliences (knives, forks, cutting board, pan, pot etc). Further all room and bathroom supplies, like bins and toilet brush etc. Which was very expensive. Came to a total of around 2000DKK

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Kitchen appliences.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Free access to the sports arena including yoga classes and other sports and a climbing wall. Also a mountaineering club and many other clubs were great.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Mountaineering club is a great way to get to hikes and places that are hard to reach by public transport or if you are unsure of venturing into the hills

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try visiting as many smaller towns as possible either for day trips of weekend. It is often duable by bus or train even it takes awhile and is totally worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Like the culture, people are friendly and good at small talk but definitely easier to make friends with other exchange students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try joining clubs or societies and going to their socials.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language and dialect at first was pretty tricky but you get the hang of it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The friendliness of strangers and general helpfulness and interest in what you were doing
there.Very
easy to go out to a pub and meet new people and smalltalk

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join clubs even if it's just one. So you have somewhere to go in the beginning if you don't click with your roommates. Say yes to coming along if people invite you even if you're a bit tired it's pretty important in the first month or so and the level will calm down.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is such a thing as Irish time. Everything may not get done right away and the bus may not always show but there is always the next one and people really don't mind if you ask them for help

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends with other students and experiencing the small towns of Ireland and going on small walks and bigger hikes. It's beautiful

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making Irish friends and finances are a bit tough with the rent.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
